Smt. Vimlesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:192649
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 21614 of 2023
Applicant :- Smt. Vimlesh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava,Shams Uz Zaman
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Ajay Nand Pandey,G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Case called out in revised list.
None present on behalf of the informant.
However, learned AGA for the State is present.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.N. Srivastava,
learned AGA for the State.
4.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 027 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Ramala, District Baghpat during pendency of the trial.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, she has been made accused in the present matter along with her other family members including husband of the deceased.

Smt. Vimlesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57114990/
1 6.

He further submits, actually applicant used to reside separately from the deceased and she was not having any concern with the family affairs of the deceased, therefore, she is not aware how deceased died.

7. He further submits, however, during post mortem cause of death of the deceased could not be ascertained and her viscera was preserved and as per instructions of learned AGA in viscera no poison was found, therefore, considering the viscera report of the deceased, it cannot be said that deceased died under abnormal circumstances and, therefore, offence under Section 304B IPC is not made out against the applicant.
8.

He further submits that applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and she is not having any criminal history and in the present matter she is in jail since 08.02.2023 i.e. for last more than one and half years.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased and there is no specific allegation against her and from the viscera report it reflects that no poison was found.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Applicant is however mother-in-law of the deceased and her daughter-in-law died within seven years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but it reflects that during post mortem cause of death of the deceased could not be ascertained and her viscera was preserved and now viscera report has been obtained by learned AGA and the same has been produced by him during the course of argument and from its perusal, it reflects that no poison was found in the viscera of the deceased

, therefore, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no evidence on record which can suggests that deceased died under abnormal circumstances.

12. Further, applicant is a lady and there is no specific allegation against her and she is not having any criminal history and in the present matter she is in jail since 08.02.2023 i.e. for last more than one and half years.
13.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant - Smt. Vimlesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Smt. Vimlesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57114990/
2
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 9.12.2024 AK Pandey  Smt. Vimlesh vs State Of U.P. on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57114990/
